title: Two's Complement Arithmetic: Subtraction, the Discarded Carry and Sign Extension
quickIdea: a - b is computed as a + (-b), that is a + inverted b + 1, and the carry out of the top bit is thrown away because the word is n bits wide.
remember: a - b = a + (invert b) + 1. One adder does both operations, which is the reason two's complement won.
The final carry out is discarded in an n-bit addition. Its presence is not the sign of the result and is not by itself an overflow.
Sign extension widens a number by copying the top bit into the new high positions, and preserves the value. Zero extension is correct only for unsigned numbers.
Read a pattern back by the weight rule: value = -b(n-1) x 2^(n-1) + sum of the lower bits' weights. No inversion is needed.
Subtracting a larger number from a smaller one gives a negative result with no borrow flag to interpret - the pattern is simply a negative two's complement number.
A hexadecimal word is read as bits first: 0xFFF5 is 1111 1111 1111 0101 before it is a number.

example.prompt: Compute 11 - 22 in 8 bits, and read the same pattern as a 16-bit word.

gateAngle: GATE CSE 2016 Set 1 Q.7 gives the 16-bit pattern 1111 1111 1111 0101 and asks for the decimal value. The two reliable routes are invert-and-add-one and the weight rule; both give -11.

variations.label: VERIFIED PYQ
variations.question: GATE CSE 2016 Set 1 Q.7: The 16-bit 2's complement representation of an integer is 1111 1111 1111 0101; its decimal representation is ______.
variations.why: Invert: 0000 0000 0000 1010; add 1: 0000 0000 0000 1011 = 11; the sign bit was 1, so the value is -11. The weight rule agrees: -32768 + 32757 = -11.

variations.label: ORIGINAL PYQ-STYLE QUESTION
variations.question: Write -100 in 16-bit two's complement, in hexadecimal.

variations.label: PREDICTED VARIATION
variations.question: The 8-bit two's complement number 0xA7 is widened to 16 bits. What is the new pattern and the value?
variations.why: 0xA7 has a 1 in the top bit, so sign extension copies ones: 1111 1111 1010 0111. Zero-extending instead would give 0x00A7 = +167, a different number - the trap the card names.

trap.what: Zero-extending a negative number, or treating the discarded carry as an overflow signal.
trap.why: The high bits of a negative two's complement number are ones, so widening must copy the sign bit. And the carry out of an n-bit addition is exactly what the modulus 2^n absorbs, so it is discarded; overflow is a statement about the sign, not about the carry.
trap.counterexample: 0xA7 as 8 bits is -89 and as 16 bits zero-extended is +167. And 0x7F + 0x01 gives 0x80 with no carry out, yet the answer -128 is not 128: that is an overflow with no carry.

check.question: In 8 bits, what is 0x0B - 0x16, and what does the pattern mean if read as unsigned?
check.explanation: 11 - 22 = -11. The same eight bits are 245 unsigned, which is 256 - 11. The pattern is fixed; only its interpretation changes.
